chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Every oath you swear upon, in which there is benefit for you regarding a matter of religion or the world, so there is no expiation upon you regarding it. And rather, the expiation falls upon you regarding what you swore upon, which is disobedience to Allah, that you do not do it, then you do it.
ai.seo_question: When does an oath require expiation (kaffarah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Reported by the prominent companion Zurarah from Imam al-Baqir, this hadith clarifies the juristic distinction between oaths for personal benefit, which are binding but incur no penalty if broken, and oaths of abstention from sin, which trigger expiation (kaffarah) upon fulfillment. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the intent behind the oath, distinguishing between casual commitments and deliberate vows to avoid disobedience. The narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the conditions under which kaffarah becomes obligatory in Shia fiqh.
